title: Subterminal agreement sheaf and its geometric stalks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a sheaf of sets on its small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], $V\to S$ an étale object, and $s,t\in F(V)$. There exists a sheaf $H$ of sets on the small étale site of $V$ such that the unique map $H\to 1$ to the terminal sheaf is a monomorphism and, for every geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the stalk $H_x$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is nonempty if and only if the germs of $s$ and $t$ at the pointed object $(V,x)$ in the stalk of $F$ at $x\to V\to S$ are equal.

source.place: Tag 09XM (lemma-where-sections-are-equal), first paragraph; Tag 03Q1 for germs under inverse image

proof.text: For a sheaf G on V and two global sections p,q, take the subfunctor of the constant singleton presheaf whose membership on U is equality of the restrictions of p,q to U. The canonical maps U to the identity étale object compose compatibly, so restriction preserves membership. Separatedness of G on the sieve of sections of this subfunctor proves the subfunctor is a sheaf, using Subfunctor.isSheaf_iff. Every section set is a subsingleton, so the unique map to the terminal sheaf is mono.

An inhabited geometric stalk has a representative on a pointed étale neighbourhood. Its membership proof gives equality of restricted sections, and germ naturality gives equality of global germs. Conversely Point.toPresheafFiber_eq_iff' witnesses equality of global germs on a pointed neighbourhood, whose agreement section produces a stalk element.

Apply the preceding construction to G = inverse image of F along V to S and to the unit images restricted along the diagonal V to V times_S V. Naturality of the germ map and pullback projection identities identify their germs under the bijective inverse-image stalk comparison with the original germs of s and t.
